items.title: 67246_Buck Clayton oral history interview
items.q: Oh boy, then I had, I was playing 'Body and Soul' and Gene Ramey trying to play a bass solo

ctx.x: Oh, and there's Spoon laying down on the floor. He says, 'you hit me!' And Emmett Berry says, 'let that be a lesson to you. Don't you never fool with musicians.' (LAUGHTER). Because he was a singer. He took up for Sir Charles because he was a musician and Jimmy Witherspoon was a singer.
Oh boy, then I had, I was playing 'Body and Soul' and Gene Ramey trying to play a bass solo and I'm holding Spoon with one hand and Emmett Berry with the other hand.
Oh Gene Ramey is playing solo.

items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: Then I went out and started working with Buck doing the, you know, gigs on weekends and things, and we went back to Europe.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah, I remember. Yeah, that's right.

I stayed with him. Then I went out and started working with Buck doing the, you know, gigs on weekends and things, and we went back to Europe. Now, this was -- by this time it was '61, and then in '62 I went with Teddy Wilson and stayed with him until I went with Earl Hines. When I left Earl Hines, I stopped over there with Eddie Condon and stayed over there until July -- September, and I quit that and took a job in the hospital for about six months, and I got the job with Chase, you know.

But in the meantime I was still playing on weekends, you know, with Buck and different groups. I even went to (The Village Streamers) Toronto with the group that made 'Fiddler on the Roof.' It had this guy, Maranyi in it, Joe Maranyi. I went there with them.
